question: What was Christine Donovan's role at Northern Trust Company and what assets did the Donor Advised Fund reach?
transcript_excerpt: Christine moved to Northern Trust Company in Chicago in 2015 and ended up building out the Donor Advised Fund, which is a philanthropic vehicle that's similar to a private foundation but a little more accessible to individuals. They brought that from about $300 million in assets up to about $1.5 to $1.7 billion.

question: Why did Christine Donovan and Adam Weems leave their corporate careers to buy Bonhoeff Ski & Sport?
transcript_excerpt: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Christine got to work from home for the first time and realized that quality of life is so much more important than the number of dollars you're making in your career. After COVID, they realized they did not like the people that they were becoming in their corporate roles. They started asking whether they liked themselves based on what they had to do, and decided they wanted to find a way to be successful in something together that brought all of their diverse career experiences together.

question: What is the history and significance of Bonhoeff Ski & Sport in Northern Michigan?
transcript_excerpt: Bonhoeff Ski & Sport was built from the ground up by Greg Smith, one of the original owners, and has been located in the Petoskey and Harbor Springs area of Northern Michigan since the early 1970s, specifically 1973. It is described as an icon in the Northern Michigan region and has 50-plus years of soul as a legacy brand.

question: What was Adam Weems' experience at the Zulgin Symbol Company and why is it notable?
transcript_excerpt: Adam worked at the Zulgin Symbol Company for about four years as the educational manager. The company turned 450 years old and is still family owned with no private equity involvement. The board of directors and last two groups of ownership have been all female, which represents a shift from the historically male-dominated leadership structure.

question: What company values did Adam Weems encounter when he moved into government software, and how did this influence his career direction?
transcript_excerpt: Adam found a company that was purpose-driven. The CEO told him: 'We have investors, though, and they know that what we're doing is the right thing. So we're going to build the right software. We are going to help modernize our governments, bringing cloud software to governments so that they can work better for us, for our people, the constituents.' This purpose-driven mission caught him and became the right way to go.
